clue.text: In retrospect, treatment almost beat illness

indicators.note: looking back, so the whole run of wordplay is read from right to left
almost the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a treatment for an ailment is a remedy
to lam is to thrash or beat

explanation.surface: Looking back, a patient reflects that the cure nearly beat the disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts REMEDY to REMED; 'In retrospect' turns REMED + LAM round to give MAL + DEMER. MAL DE MER is French for seasickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mal de mer is the French phrase for seasickness, a nauseous complaint suffered by sea travellers.

clue.text: You'll find in Miami a smattering of pollution

definitions.note: an abstract noun for the foul vapour itself

indicators.note: the letters are found sitting within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Visitors to a Florida city encounter a little smog.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is a noxious, polluting vapour once thought to spread disease.

clue.text: Hurriedly leave the Middle East

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to depart the region in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To levant is old slang for absconding to dodge debts; the Levant is the eastern Mediterranean region.

clue.text: Ring English officer, a redcap, on a ship

parts.note: NCO is a non-commissioned officer
a redcap is British slang for a military policeman, an MP
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An English soldier and a military policeman phone someone aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call, but it is a verb meaning surround.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to surround or encircle, as a ring does.

clue.text: Declining to answer, does withdraw

indicators.note: the fodder's letters decline, in the sense of being inflected into another shape

explanation.surface: Someone who refuses to reply does pull out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat your words is to retract a statement, admitting it was wrong.

clue.text: Fruits for Joyce

definitions.note: William Joyce, the wartime Nazi broadcaster, was nicknamed Lord Haw-Haw

parts.note: haws are the red berries of the hawthorn, so two of them give the pair
haws are the red berries of the hawthorn, so two of them give the pair

explanation.surface: Someone offers fruit to a person called Joyce.
explanation.walkthrough: William Joyce broadcast Nazi propaganda to Britain in World War II and was mocked as Lord Haw-Haw for his drawling, affected voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Haw-Haw was the derisive nickname British listeners gave the traitor broadcaster William Joyce.

clue.text: Shot, in some pain

indicators.note: the word for a shot is placed inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any?
a go is an attempt, a shot at something

explanation.surface: A wounded man reports being shot and in some pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Agony is extreme physical or mental suffering.

clue.text: Famous choir — it's disbanded

indicators.note: the singers scatter, so the letters break up and reform

explanation.surface: A celebrated choir announces it has broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means important or renowned enough to be remembered in history.

clue.text: We will take trouble to get comfortable

parts.note: we'll is the contraction of we will
a to-do is a fuss or bother

explanation.surface: We will go to great pains to be at ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do means prosperous, comfortably off.

clue.text: Recommend a lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a solicitor to be suggested.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to urge or support an idea; an advocate is also a barrister who pleads cases in court, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Antiquated vessel sunk in defeat

definitions.note: an adjective here, matching the answer used attributively for something hopelessly outdated

indicators.note: the ship's letters are submerged within the word for defeat

parts.note: to foil a plan is to defeat it
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An old ship goes down after losing a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil, as a modifier, describes something petrified and hopelessly out of date, like an old fogey.

clue.text: One seat held by people in the Establishment

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the seat is contained within the word for people

parts.note: a nation is a people
a stall is a theatre seat

explanation.surface: A single seat is occupied by members of the ruling class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Establishment' suggests the ruling elite, but it means a base or facility; 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An installation is a military or industrial establishment, such as a base.

clue.text: Make a note of little number

explanation.surface: Someone is told to jot down a small figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' and 'of' are linking words around the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth two crotchets, and also a tiny liquid measure, one sixtieth of a fluid drachm.

clue.text: Kids' mother responsible for attack on child-minder

indicators.note: in a down-the-page or after sense, the attack comes following the child-minder

parts.note: a nanny is a woman employed to look after children
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A mother blames a nanny for an assault on her children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kids' looks like children, but they are young goats; 'responsible for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Young goats are called kids, and their female parent is the she-goat.

clue.text: Sailors whistle to get some money

explanation.surface: Seamen whistle in hope of earning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Old sailors whistled believing it would summon a breeze on a calm day; the phrase also means to raise funds for a venture.

clue.text: "The Last of The Revenger" adapted for the box, for example

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken
the play title is adapted, rearranged into new form

explanation.surface: The end of a Jacobean revenge drama is adapted for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the box' seems to be TV, but it is the box shrub, an example of a plant that keeps its leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Box is a hedging shrub that keeps its foliage all year, so it is an example of such a plant.

clue.text: I cry when you're listening, sweet

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is heard and a phrase spoken alike is entered

parts.note: I cry out could be I scream

explanation.surface: Someone weeps whenever you pay attention, darling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' looks like a term of endearment, but it is a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dairy dessert is a pudding, which British English calls a sweet.

clue.text: Change I give a close friend

parts.note: to alter is to change
ego is Latin for I, the self

explanation.surface: I hand over some money to a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego, literally another self, can mean an intimate companion.

clue.text: Slight indisposition to bear

parts.note: a cold is a minor ailment or indisposition
to shoulder a burden is to bear it

explanation.surface: Someone has a mild illness they must put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' reads as an adjective qualifying the illness, but it is the definition, meaning a snub.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone the frosty treatment is a deliberate snub, an intentional slight.

clue.text: Lady carrying on home for gentlemen

indicators.note: the lady's name carries, so holds, the word on inside it

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman keeps going on about a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen came from this Italian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona names the city as their home town.

clue.text: Case not in position

indicators.note: not with the word in means that word is taken away

parts.note: an instance is a case or example

explanation.surface: A suitcase is not where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a posture or standpoint.

clue.text: Water-clock worked in dry places

indicators.note: worked like dough, the letters are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: A water-clock was operated in arid regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A clepsydra is an ancient timekeeper that measured hours by the steady flow of liquid through a hole.

clue.text: Scandinavian vegetable

explanation.surface: A Nordic root crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede comes from Sweden; a swede is also a yellow-fleshed turnip-like root, called rutabaga in North America.

clue.text: Big jar, by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells us the word for jar is heard, and a word spoken the same way is entered

parts.note: to jar on the nerves is to grate

explanation.surface: Someone describes a large storage pot judging by its noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Great is a straightforward synonym of large or huge.

clue.text: The Spanish still provide a team

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine word for the
still and even are both used as intensifiers: still better, even better

explanation.surface: Spaniards nonetheless field a side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or football side has that many players, so the number names a team.

clue.text: Philip and Edward have to shut up

parts.note: Pip is a short form of Philip, as in Great Expectations
Ed is a short form of Edward
to own is to have or possess

explanation.surface: Two men named Philip and Edward are told they must be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal order to stop talking, from the bosun's whistle signalling lights out.

clue.text: Low fellow put forward

parts.note: to low is the noise cattle make, as is moo
Ted is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A humble man was promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: To moot a topic is to raise it for discussion, to propose it.

clue.text: I'll get an appointment after one in order to overrun

indicators.note: the appointment comes after the religious sister in the word

parts.note: I'll is I will, so I gets the letter I
a nun is a member of a religious order
a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: Someone books a meeting for just after one o'clock so as to run late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' seems to mean sequence, but it is a religious order; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or swamp, overwhelming a place as an invading force overruns it.
